llm.summary: The skill's code, runtime instructions, and requested environment variables are consistent with a Withings API client for multiple family members; it only asks for Withings client credentials and stores per-user OAuth tokens locally.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to fetch Withings health data and the included Python scripts implement OAuth and calls to Withings endpoints (account.withings.com, wbsapi.withings.net). The only required env vars are WITHINGS_CLIENT_ID and WITHINGS_CLIENT_SECRET, which are appropriate and proportional for this purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions and scripts remain narrowly scoped to Withings OAuth and API calls and to reading/writing token files in ~/.openclaw/withings-family (or legacy path). Minor documentation inconsistencies exist: SKILL.md mentions storing client credentials in a .env file while the scripts load config.json or environment variables, the oauth helper module docstring references localhost:8080 but the code uses port 18081, and some endpoints/paths vary between scripts — these are functional/documentation mismatches rather than scope creep. The scripts do start a local HTTP callback server on localhost (default port 18081) for OAuth, which is expected for this flow.

dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only skill + shipped Python scripts). Required binary is python3, which is reasonable. Nothing is downloaded from arbitrary URLs or installed automatically.

dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only WITHINGS_CLIENT_ID and WITHINGS_CLIENT_SECRET are required, matching the skill's stated need to authenticate to Withings. The scripts also optionally load a local config.json in the skill directory; no other secrets, system credentials, or unrelated environment variables are requested or accessed.

dimensions.detail: always:false and user-invocable:true (normal). The skill stores per-user token files under the user's home directory and attempts to set permissions to 600 — this is expected behavior for OAuth token storage and the skill does not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it performs Withings OAuth and fetches metrics, and it only requests Withings client credentials. Before installing, consider these practical checks: 1) Verify you trust the skill source (the repo URL) because the scripts will store OAuth tokens in ~/.openclaw/withings-family/tokens-<user>.json; the files are written locally and the code attempts chmod 600 but behavior differs on Windows. 2) Set WITHINGS_CLIENT_ID and WITHINGS_CLIENT_SECRET as environment variables (the scripts prefer env or a config.json in the skill folder — SKILL.md mentions a .env file but the code reads config.json). 3) The OAuth helper starts a local HTTP listener on localhost:18081 to capture the authorization code; ensure that port is available and that you are comfortable opening a browser to the Withings authorize URL. 4) The scripts contact only account.withings.com and wbsapi.withings.net; if you see network calls to other domains, stop and inspect. 5) Because there are small doc/port/file-name inconsistencies, follow the code (not only the README) when configuring. Running the scripts in a local/isolated environment (or inspecting them yourself) is recommended if you have any doubts.
